correctness.rationale: Arbitrary one-coordinate antiderivative tests give the three stated conditional regressions. Stationarity of \(x^2\) and of \(z\) yields \(\mathbb E[z]=\mathbb E[x^2]=\mathbb E[xy]\), and \(c>0\) excludes zero height. The regression residual \(y-x=\dot x/\sigma\) gives the exact variance defect. Differentiating \(x^2/\sigma+y^2+z^2\) gives the shell \(\operatorname{Var}(z)+s=h(r-1-h)+cm\). Cauchy–Schwarz reduces nonnegativity of the shell to the cubic inequality for \(q=\sqrt h\), whose unique positive root is the positive equilibrium amplitude. Equality forces zero variances and zero speed defect, hence the positive equilibrium atom. The packaged checker replays the polynomial and numerical-root calculations.

value.rationale: The Ehrhard–Müller system is a physically derived convection-loop model whose literature emphasizes coexistence and transitions among steady, periodic, and chaotic regimes. The theorem supplies an exact attractor-independent calibration: mean thermal height equals the fast-variable mean square, while mismatch between the two fast variables appears as a measurable speed defect in the stationary shell. The shell then yields a sharp parameter-only RMS ceiling equal to the positive equilibrium amplitude, with a rigid equality case. At the published chaotic example this gives a concrete exact upper bound on the stationary mean height and fast RMS, so the result is directly usable as a consistency check for long-time numerical or experimental statistics across different recurrent regimes.
